nodes.name: Dawn of the Hunt
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access update 0.2.0 (launched 2025-04-04) and its temporary league. It added Azmeri wisps, rogue exiles and idols to the core game; not officially a full league.

sources.locator: lead: launched April 4, 2025 as part of Path of Exile 2: Dawn of the Hunt, version 0.2.0; ended August 26, 2025

nodes.name: The Third Edict (0.3.0)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access update 0.3.0 (2025-08-29): added Act 4 (Kingsmarch, Ngamakanui, hunt for the Weapon/instrument of the Third Edict), three Interludes, removal of Cruel difficulty, and Rise of the Abyssal league.

sources.locator: Act Four continues from Act 3 ... Doryani agrees to help find an ancient weapon, the instrument of the Third Edict; three Interludes lead to level 65 where endgame begins; Cruel removed

nodes.name: Rise of the Abyssal
nodes.summary: First 'full' PoE2 league (0.3.0, 2025-08-29 to 2025-12-09): Abyssal fissures open as green cracks near monster packs; closing them reveals an Abyssal Trove and sometimes the Abyssal Depths; preserved bones feed desecration at the Well of Souls (Act 2).

nodes.name: The Last of the Druids (0.4.0)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access update 0.4.0 (2025-12-12): added the Druid class, the Fate of the Vaal league, many support gems and endgame changes.

sources.locator: released December 12, 2025 with Druid class and Fate of the Vaal league
lead: launched December 12, 2025 as part of The Last of the Druids, version 0.4.0

nodes.name: Fate of the Vaal
nodes.summary: 0.4.0 temporary league centred on Atziri's Temple (Lira Vaal): Ancient Beacons, the Temple Console, Royal Architect Xipocado and Queen Atziri; later moved into the core game (see 0.5 'Fate of the Vaal moving to core').

nodes.name: Return of the Ancients (0.5.0)
nodes.summary: PoE2 update 0.5.0 (2026-05-29), final major pre-1.0 patch: rebuilt Atlas with fixed storylines, Precursor Fortress, Atlas Masters, Runes of Aldur league, Spirit Walker and Martial Artist ascendancies.

sources.locator: lead: launched May 29, 2026 as part of Path of Exile 2: Return of the Ancients, version 0.5.0

nodes.name: Runes of Aldur
nodes.summary: 0.5.0 temporary league: Farrow studies runes on Verisium Remnants (Ezomyte Runesmithing with Kalguuran origins), producing Runic Ward, Kalguuran gems and alloys; folded into the core game with Expedition in 0.5.5.

sources.locator: Runes of Aldur (Runesmithing): Farrow, a young blacksmith, reveals the Kalguuran origins of Ezomyte Runesmithing

nodes.name: Forbidden Rites (0.5.5)
nodes.summary: 0.5.5 event league (2026-09-04) running beside Runes of Aldur: Ritual encounters in every campaign and endgame zone, unique-boss Ritual clusters per act, Viridian Wildwood via Sacred Bloom; integrates Runes of Aldur and Expedition into core.

nodes.name: Atlas of Worlds (PoE2)
nodes.summary: The PoE2 endgame map network, reached after the campaign via Doryani's Waygate and navigated with Waystones. Rebuilt in 0.5 (Return of the Ancients) with fixed points of interest, storylines and a fully unlockable Atlas passive tree.

sources.locator: quest log: 'Use the Map Device and the Waystone to enter a Map'
Atlas passive tree: Fully remade; zone quest chains

nodes.name: Waygate (Map Device)
nodes.summary: Machine at the Ziggurat Refuge that Doryani calls a 'Waygate': built over underground leylines, it can take the Exile anywhere the leylines reach; a Waystone placed in it opens a Map. The wiki quest text does not say who built it (the earlier draft's 'Precursor-built' is unsupported).

sources.locator: Doryani: 'The machine you see here... I call it... a Waygate. Using the leylines, the Waygate can take us anywhere they reach.'

nodes.name: Leylines
nodes.summary: Ancient underground structures Doryani believes span the continent beneath the Ziggurat; they power the Waygate and resonate with the Precursor Tower.

sources.locator: Doryani: This Ziggurat was built over what my ancestors called 'leylines'

nodes.name: Waystone
nodes.summary: Item Doryani gives the Exile to mark coordinates and place in the Waygate to open a Map; the key mechanic of the PoE2 Atlas.

sources.locator: Doryani: 'Take this Waystone. Mark your desired coordinates on it. Place it in the Waygate.'

nodes.name: The Ziggurat Refuge
nodes.summary: Endgame hub (the wiki also calls it the Ziggurat Encampment) where Doryani keeps the Waygate; the Ziggurat stands over what his ancestors called leylines. Quest Siege of Oriath ends with the Exile arriving here.

sources.locator: Take a Waystone from Doryani in The Ziggurat Refuge

nodes.name: Legacy of the Precursors (endgame quest)
nodes.summary: The primary PoE2 endgame quest: the Hooded One sleeps, held in thrall by the Beast's Corruption; Doryani proposes recovering Precursor knowledge via the Waygate, leading to the Precursor Tower, the Fortress, the Burning Monolith, the Arbiter of Ash and (0.5) the Arbiter of Divinity.

chronology.relative: Immediately after the PoE2 campaign (post-Siege of Oriath)

sources.locator: lead: primary endgame quest obtained immediately upon reaching the endgame; quest log 'Check on the Hooded One' / 'Speak to Doryani'

nodes.name: Testing the Waygate
nodes.summary: Doryani has the Exile run the first Waystone map; he had not tested the Waygate beforehand ('Science is a process').

sources.locator: quest steps 'Select and enter a Map' / Doryani 'Our first step is a success! The Waygate does indeed work.'

nodes.name: Activating the Precursor Tower
nodes.summary: The Exile reaches a Precursor Tower and activates its beacon; an Irradiated Tablet drops and (in 0.5) the Precursor Fortress rises from the ground in a cinematic.

sources.locator: Activate the Precursor Beacon: 'An Irradiated Tablet will drop, and the Precursor Fortress will rise from the ground in a cinematic.'

nodes.name: Ancient Gateway and the Fortress Gateways
nodes.summary: After the Fortress rises, the Exile travels to the Ancient Gateway, uses levers to reach the central platform, summons Doryani and activates another Precursor Beacon, which opens the way to the Burning Monolith (quest log, Legacy of the Precursors).

sources.locator: quest log: 'Travel to the Ancient Gateway', 'Defeat the Precursor Separator', 'Ride the Elevator'

nodes.name: The Burning Monolith
nodes.summary: Endgame site reached during Legacy of the Precursors ('Reach the Burning Monolith') after the Ancient Gateway. In 0.1-0.4 it was found directly on the Atlas and opened with three Crisis Fragments (The Pinnacle of Flame); in 0.5 it stands inside the Precursor Fortress.

sources.locator: 'Reach the Burning Monolith', 'Return to the Burning Monolith'
Find The Burning Monolith on the endgame map; obtain three Crisis Fragments to open the locked door

nodes.name: Western and Eastern Gateways, Enigma Chambers: Count Geonor and Doryani
nodes.summary: From the Burning Monolith the Exile clears the Western Gateway (guardian: Precursor Separator) and Eastern Gateway (Precursor Refiner) via levers, then fights Count Geonor in the Western Enigma Chamber (Ancient Crisis Fragment) and Doryani in the Eastern Enigma Chamber (Weathered Crisis Fragment) (quest log; this section of the wiki log is in a hidden comment block, so medium confidence). The Doryani and Geonor fights echo the Citadel bosses of 0.1-0.4.

sources.locator: 'Defeat Count Geonor', 'Defeat Doryani', 'Pick up the Ancient Crisis Fragment', 'Pick up the Weathered Crisis Fragment'
Enigma Chambers drop the two Crisis Fragments

nodes.name: Defeating the Arbiter of Ash
nodes.summary: The Exile kills the Arbiter of Ash at the Burning Monolith. In 0.5 it is a quest boss inside the Fortress and no longer the apex; afterwards a mysterious rider on a wyrm (Tecrod) steals the Flame Seed.

sources.locator: Lore: Mysterious Entity riding a wyrm steals the Flame Seed after the Arbiter of Ash is defeated

nodes.name: The Origin Core and the Origin Tower
nodes.summary: Combining the Origin Cradle and Origin Spark (from the Matriarch and Patriarch Halls) in the Precursor Reactor yields the Origin Core; when the Exile places it in the Origin Tower, Tecrod's wyrm incapacitates the Exile and Tecrod exults 'With this, the Master shall know unending power!' before the Arbiter of Divinity destroys his body.

sources.locator: Lore: when the player places the Origin Core into the Origin Tower, Tecrod's wyrm incapacitates the character
Matriarch and Patriarch Halls drop Origin Cradle and Origin Spark; combine into Origin Core at the Precursor Reactor

nodes.name: Defeating the Arbiter of Divinity
nodes.summary: At the top of the Origin Tower the Exile fights the Arbiter of Divinity (quest step 141); quest complete: 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'

sources.locator: his body is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity

nodes.name: The Pinnacle of Flame (removed quest)
nodes.summary: Epilogue/endgame quest of 0.1-0.4: find the Burning Monolith on the endgame map and collect three Crisis Fragments to open the door to the Arbiter of Ash. Removed in 0.5.0 and folded into Legacy of the Precursors.

sources.locator: Walkthrough and Version history: 0.1.0 introduced, 0.5.0 removed

nodes.name: The Arbiter of Ash
nodes.summary: Guardian of the Flame Seed, created by the Precursors (PoE wiki, History of Wraeclast; the PoE2 wiki says the Unblinking Eye most likely subjugated it originally, which is speculative). Sealed at the Burning Monolith; fought by the Exile as PoE2's first Atlas pinnacle (0.1-0.4) and as a Fortress quest boss in 0.5, after which a wyrm-rider (Tecrod) steals the Flame Seed. Little else is known.

sources.locator: most likely the original subjugation of the Arbiter of Ash
Precursors: 'They also created the Arbiter of Ash (PoE 2) to guard the Flame Seed (PoE 2)'; 'Little is known about the Arbiter and the Flame Seed'

nodes.name: The Arbiter of Divinity
nodes.summary: Boss atop the Origin Tower, fought after the Origin Core is placed; it destroys Tecrod's body ('Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!') and ends the threat of the First Edict. The wiki does not say what it is (the 'apex of the Origins of Divinity storyline' framing comes from guides); 0.5.4 patches later adjusted the fight.

sources.locator: 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'
boss guide: final boss of the Origins of Divinity storyline

nodes.name: Tecrod, the Hated Slave
nodes.summary: White-haloed Abyssal Lich Lord ('the Hated Slave'). The PoE2 wiki says that, unlike Amanamu, Kurgal and Ulaman, he acts independently of Kulemak's other lords and is active in the Epilogue hunting the Edicts; the PoE wiki adds he was forsaken by Kulemak, is freed from a Precursor sarcophagus and seeks to win back Kulemak's favour. He steals the Flame Seed, incapacitates the Exile at the Origin Tower claiming the First Edict's power for 'the Master' (probably Kulemak, inferred), and is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity.

sources.locator: Lich Lords: Tecrod, the disgraced Abyssal Lich, forsaken by Kulemak; freed from a Precursor sarcophagus, seeks to win back Kulemak favour

nodes.name: Flame Seed
nodes.summary: Object guarded by the Arbiter of Ash (Precursor-made guardian); after the Arbiter dies a mysterious wyrm-rider, later revealed as Tecrod, takes it saying 'This power serves a new master...'.

sources.locator: A Mysterious Entity riding a wyrm that steals the Flame Seed ... 'This power serves a new master...'

nodes.name: Origin Core
nodes.summary: 0.5 key item assembled from the Origin Cradle and Origin Spark; placed into the Origin Tower to open the way to the Arbiter of Divinity.

sources.locator: Matriarch and Patriarch Halls drop Origin Cradle and Origin Spark; combine into Origin Core
places the Origin Core into the Origin Tower

nodes.name: The Burning Monolith
nodes.summary: Site where the Arbiter of Ash is fought; in 0.1-0.4 a door on the Atlas opened by three Crisis Fragments, in 0.5 moved inside the Precursor Fortress.

sources.locator: Three Crisis Fragments, one from each Citadel, open the Burning Monolith

nodes.name: The Precursor Fortress
nodes.summary: Vast Precursor structure that rises from the ground when the first Precursor Beacon is activated (0.5); contains the Ancient/Western/Eastern Gateways, Enigma Chambers, the Burning Monolith, the Halls and the Origin Tower. Official 0.5.0 notes: 'The Cataclysm of the Beast has invoked an ancient protocol'; players seek keys to reach and disarm ancient Precursor weapons.

sources.locator: Activate the Precursor Beacon: Fortress will rise from the ground
Origins of Divinity: ancient protocol; obtain keys to reach the Precursor weapons and disarm them

nodes.name: The Origin Tower
nodes.summary: Tower at the Fortress core where the Origin Core is placed and the Arbiter of Divinity is fought.

sources.locator: area: the Burning Monolith, the Origin Tower

nodes.name: Crisis Fragments
nodes.summary: Fragments needed to open the sealed door of the Burning Monolith (Arbiter of Ash). In 0.1-0.4 three were needed (Ancient, Weathered, Faded), one per Citadel boss. In the 0.5 quest log only the Ancient and Weathered fragments are picked up in the Fortress Enigma Chambers; Citadels continue to drop them for repeat runs. Guides disagree on which Citadel drops which (most: Iron=Ancient, Copper=Faded, Stone=Weathered), and the quest log matches that for Geonor (Ancient) and Doryani (Weathered).

sources.locator: Citadel-to-Arbiter loop; fragment mapping disagrees between guides

nodes.name: Citadels (Iron, Copper, Stone)
nodes.summary: Three Atlas fortresses (Iron, Copper, Stone) whose bosses drop one Crisis Fragment each toward the Arbiter of Ash: Iron Citadel = Count Geonor, Copper Citadel = Jamanra, Stone Citadel = Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge (agreed by several guides; the poe2 wiki Doryani page also lists the Stone Citadel). The removed 0.1-0.4 epilogue quests Faridun Foray (boss listed Count Geonor), Ezomyte Infiltration (boss listed The Perennial King) and Vaal Incursion (boss Doryani) all start 'Investigate the Burning Monolith'; how The Perennial King maps to Jamanra is unclear. Fragment mapping differs between guides.

sources.locator: quest infobox: boss Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge; start 'Investigate The Burning Monolith'; removed 0.5.0
quest infobox: boss Count Geonor; removed 0.5.0
quest infobox: boss The Perennial King; removed 0.5.0
can be found in endgame as a citadel boss in The Stone Citadel
Stone (Doryani), Copper (Jamanra), Iron (Count Geonor) - fragment mapping differs from other guides

nodes.name: The Unblinking Eye
nodes.summary: Mysterious group associated with the Templars involved in notable events in Wraeclast's history.

nodes.name: Masters of the Atlas
nodes.summary: 0.5 storylines of three Atlas Masters: Jado (Order of the Djinn; unlocked by an anomaly map near the start), Hilda (monster hunter, Hilda's Campsite) and Doryani (unlocked by clearing a corruption nexus). The earlier draft's 'ascendancy-like specialisation' claim is unsupported and was removed.

sources.locator: Atlas Masters: Jado, Hilda, Doryani; Doryani questline via corruption nexus; Jado via anomaly map

nodes.name: Jado
nodes.summary: Member of the Order of the Djinn first met in Interlude 2; reveals Jun has been rebuilding the Order in secret for 20 years since Catarina's fall. Atlas Master in 0.5, unlocked via an anomaly map near the Atlas start.

sources.locator: first mentioned by Jado, NPC introduced in Interlude 2
Atlas Masters: Jado of the Order of the Djinn
Jado questline unlocked by completing an anomaly map near the starting location

nodes.name: Hilda
nodes.summary: Monster hunter and Atlas Master (Hilda's Campsite); her endgame quest Hilda's Hunting has the Exile track and defeat four Great Beasts.

sources.locator: Atlas Masters: Hilda, a monster hunter
Quest Complete: 'You have tracked and defeated four Great Beasts.'

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Secret order founded by the Maraketh to guard relics and protect Wraeclast; nearly destroyed by Janus's betrayal in PoE1's Betrayal; Jun rebuilds it in secret, per PoE2.

nodes.name: Jun Ortoi
nodes.summary: Veteran Order of the Djinn member; in PoE2 mentioned as rebuilding the Order since Catarina's fall 20 years earlier.

nodes.name: Kulemak
nodes.summary: Lich Lord, creator and master of the Lightless, exalted in the Well of Souls; the Hooded One calls him 'a dark god... Kulemak, the Lich Lord, master of Undeath' whose body the alliance destroyed countless times though the Well stayed out of reach. Fought as the Vessel of Kulemak via Kulemak's Invitation in the Black Cathedral.

sources.locator: Hooded One: 'Kulemak, the Lich Lord, master of Undeath'

nodes.name: The Lightless (Abyssals)
nodes.summary: Ancient necromantic race, the Abyssals ('the spawn of the Well of Souls' per the Hooded One), serving Kulemak through Lich Lords; they emerge through Abyss fissures. Ancient alliances fought them for centuries in the Winter of the World.

nodes.name: Amanamu, Liege of the Lightless
nodes.summary: Lich Lord under Kulemak; boss of the Abyssal Depths.

sources.locator: Lich Lords who serve under Kulemak - Amanamu, Kurgal, and Ulaman

nodes.name: Kurgal, the Blackblooded
nodes.summary: Lich Lord under Kulemak; a Delve boss in PoE1 (The Lich's Tomb, depth 90+) and named as a PoE2 Lich Lord by the Lurking Creature.

nodes.name: Ulaman, Sovereign of the Well
nodes.summary: Lich Lord under Kulemak; Abyssal Depths boss.

nodes.name: The Well of Souls
nodes.summary: Wellspring of necromancy that collects all souls; Kulemak's seat. In PoE2 reached via the Lightless Passage from Mastodon Badlands in Act 2; later the Abyss hub.

nodes.name: The Black Cathedral
nodes.summary: Level-80 area off the Well of Souls entered only with Kulemak's Invitation; site of the Kulemak encounter.

sources.locator: area table: The Black Cathedral 80 - Kulemak's Invitation

nodes.name: Lurking Creature
nodes.summary: Abyssal being at the Well of Souls who calls the Exile 'Thief of Virtue! Stealer of Kulemak's spark!', serves whoever holds Kulemak's dominion (Amanamu, Ulaman, Kurgal) but never Tecrod.

nodes.name: The Exile discovers the Well of Souls
nodes.summary: In Act 2 the Exile follows Abyssal fissures into the Lightless Passage; the Hooded One teaches them the Abyssal tongue and names Kulemak.

nodes.name: Vessel of Kulemak
nodes.summary: Pinnacle Abyss encounter, the Vessel of Kulemak: Kulemak's Invitation (dropped by Abyssal commanders per guides) sends the player into the Well and the Black Cathedral. Guides say defeating it unlocks the Abyssal Lich ascendancy (exact conditions vary by guide/patch); fully empowering it means defeating the Lich Lords Kurgal, Ulaman and Amanamu.

sources.locator: Vessel of Kulemak: Tasgul and Vandroth drop Kulemak Invitation; empower via Kurgal, Ulaman, Amanamu

nodes.name: Abyssal Depths (PoE2)
nodes.summary: Underground realm accessed from some Abyss fissures; in 0.5 three Abyssal faction bosses guard it and yield the key to the Well of Souls (community guide).

sources.locator: League content: access to the Abyssal Depths

nodes.name: Trial of Chaos
nodes.summary: Ascension trial in the Temple of Chaos (first in Act 3), a gauntlet run with an Inscribed Ultimatum; the Trialmaster offers modifiers and rewards. Mechanically based on PoE1's Ultimatum.

nodes.name: The Trialmaster
nodes.summary: Servant of Chaos who runs the Trial: 'My master, Chaos, has charged me with this task.'

nodes.name: Trial of the Sekhemas
nodes.summary: Ascension trial first accessible in Act 2 via a Djinn Barya on the Relic Altar; a gauntlet governed by Honour, Boons and Afflictions; based on PoE1's Forbidden Sanctum.

nodes.name: Balbala, the Traitor
nodes.summary: Act 2 boss in Traitor's Passage whose barya (Balbala's Barya) holds her soul and is the quest key to the Trial of the Sekhemas.

sources.locator: Shambrin: Her barya contains her soul

nodes.name: Atziri's Temple (Lira Vaal)
nodes.summary: Past version of the temple unlocked via Ancient Beacons; the present ruin is the Lost Temple. Built via the Temple Console; Doryani turns the entrance into a time portal after Act 3/4.

sources.locator: lead; Ancient Beacon; Doryani will activate the time portal

nodes.name: Xipocado, Royal Architect
nodes.summary: Boss of Atziri's Temple; in PoE1 an enemy in past Temple of Atzoatl who built the Royal Meeting Room to Atziri's throne.

nodes.name: Fate of the Vaal (quest)
nodes.summary: Quest (0.4 league): with Doryani and Alva the Exile uses the Temple Console to open Atziri's Temple (Doryani turns the entrance into a time portal), defeats Xipocado and the Royal Architect, then Atziri the Red Queen and Atziri the Fell Serpent in The Cradle, and takes Atziri's Medallion; the wiki's completion text: you failed to stop the Vaal Cataclysm.

chronology.relative: Quest obtained in Act 4 after unlocking Atziri's Temple and recruiting Doryani (0.4 league)

sources.locator: Quest Complete: 'You have defeated Atziri, the Red Queen... but you failed to stop the Vaal Cataclysm.'

nodes.name: Ancient Beacons
nodes.summary: Vaal devices that fuel Atziri's Temple when monsters are sacrificed to them; six open a portal to the Vaal Ruins.

nodes.name: Azmeri Spirits and Wisps
nodes.summary: Azmeri spirits appear as wisps leading hunters to monsters, introduced with Dawn of the Hunt; Delwyn at Hunting Grounds teaches the hunt; the Spirit Walker ascendancy (0.5) controls Stag, Owl, Bear spirits.

sources.locator: Spirit Walker (Huntress) master of Azmeri spirits

nodes.name: Delwyn
nodes.summary: Azmeri hunter in the Hunting Grounds who introduces the Azmerian wisp hunts; recognises the Huntress.

nodes.name: Rogue Exiles (PoE2)
nodes.summary: Roaming exile NPC bosses introduced in 0.2.0; Abyss can raise a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile.

sources.locator: raising a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile

nodes.name: Breach and the Keepers of the Flame (PoE2 0.5)
nodes.summary: 0.5 Breach storyline: Ailith and the Keepers of the Flame hold back the Hiveborn from the Monastery of the Keepers; the Genesis Tree is a crafting hub; endgame Breach Domains end in Sky Fortresses with the Breachlords Tul and Esh, then Xesht.

sources.locator: Breach: Ailith and the Keepers of the Flame hold back the Hiveborn

nodes.name: Ailith
nodes.summary: Founder of the Order of the Purple Flame / Keepers of the Flame after visions of the Dreamer (PoE1 Keepers); in PoE2 0.5 she leads the Breach questline against the Hiveborn, defends the Sky Hive domain closure and is a preserved essence/copy kept by the Dreamer, who has become somewhat self-aware. 'Alith' is a guide misspelling.

sources.locator: Lore: Ailith founded the Order; she is a copy the Dreamer keeps; PoE2 version aware of her nature
Sky Hives: defend Ailith while she closes the domain

nodes.name: Keepers of the Flame
nodes.summary: Cult formed in Chayula's dreams, dedicated to destroying the Hiveborn; based at the Monastery of the Keepers.

nodes.name: Hiveborn
nodes.summary: Breach-spawn into which the Breachlords were evolving; the Keepers of the Flame, founded through Chayula's dreams, exist to destroy them. The Dreamer is revealed to be of the same kind as the Hiveborn.

sources.locator: Lore: the Breachlords began their evolution into the Hiveborn; the Dreamer is the same creature as the Hiveborn

nodes.name: Monastery of the Keepers
nodes.summary: Southern Atlas site; hidden chamber houses the Dreamer; Genesis Tree and Grasping Orchid located here.

sources.locator: hidden area in the Monastery of the Keepers
Monastery of the Keepers to grow a Grasping Orchid

nodes.name: Vruun, Marshal of Xesht
nodes.summary: Breach boss in Unstable Breach encounters; drops the Head of Vruun used to grow the Grasping Orchid; introduced 0.5.0.

nodes.name: Chayula, the Dreamer
nodes.summary: Breachlord known as the Dreamer or Benevolent Dreamer; PoE2 lore shows he aided the Third Pact alliance, was severed from the failed Breachlord merge, and formed the Keepers of the Flame through dreams. After Xesht falls Ailith reveals his ultimate aim is to subjugate all life as obedient thralls.

sources.locator: Lore: after Xesht is defeated Ailith tells the player the Dreamer's true intent

nodes.name: Waking the Dreamer
nodes.summary: 0.5 Breach story: travel to the Monastery of the Keepers and the Genesis Tree; defeat It That Was Tul and It That Was Esh (Sky Fortress bosses; official notes: they yield the key to the Breach pinnacle) and retrieve the Breachlord Sac to reach the Dreamer; later fight Xesht. Hiveborn details come from press coverage.

sources.locator: After defeating It That Was Esh and It That Was Tul and retrieving the Breachlord Sac
Tul and Esh are fortress bosses; defeating them yields a key to the Breach Pinnacle boss

nodes.name: Ritual and the King in the Mists (PoE2)
nodes.summary: 0.5 Ritual storyline: Aoife, a lost spirit bound by the King in the Mists, appeals to the Wildwood; the prison beneath holds the Bodach; the Rite of the Nameless in Caer Tarth. 0.5.5 adds Ritual altars to every zone.

sources.locator: Ritual: Aoife, a lost spirit, bound by the King in the Mists... Bodach ... Rite of the Nameless

nodes.name: The King in the Mists
nodes.summary: Boss who killed Aoife and whose effigies tether him to the world; killed once in the campaign (Ogham) yet returns in the endgame Ritual quest, where he is fought at the Crux of Nothingness; his Head starts the Rite of the Nameless. Drawing power from the Bodach is a guide claim.

sources.locator: Aoife: 'You killed him in your domain... but now he returns from his'; step 17 Defeat the King in the Mists; step 20 Pick up the Head of the King
Killing the King drops The Head of the King, which starts the Rite of the Nameless in Caer Tarth

nodes.name: Aoife
nodes.summary: Spirit of a woman killed by the King in the Mists (the 'King of the Nameless'), who once drew her and the Druid in as a supposed Maji; she appears near a Ritual Altar in a map, bound to the Wildwood/Caer Tarth area, and asks the Exile to destroy the King's effigies. She is the Druid's lost love (Druid dialogue: 'Aoife? You return to me once more!'). She is laid to rest after the Bodach falls.

sources.locator: Aoife: 'Killed by the King of the Nameless... The King in the Mists'; Quest Complete
Aoife lingers as a restless spirit, bound to the Wildwood

nodes.name: The Bodach
nodes.summary: Dark entity fought as the final boss of Legacy of the Maji after the Rite of the Nameless ('Explore the Darkness'; 'Defeat the Bodach'); the official 0.5.0 text says a prison beneath Caer Tarth holds it. At T14+ it is the Ritual pinnacle per a guide.

sources.locator: steps 53-54 'Explore the Darkness', 'Defeat the Bodach'; completion: Defeat The Bodach
The prison beneath it holds the Bodach

nodes.name: Viridian Wildwood
